title: Carbon monoxide
tldr: If a CO alarm sounds or carbon monoxide exposure is suspected, get everyone into fresh air immediately and call emergency services. Do not stay inside to find the source. Headache, dizziness, nausea or confusion can be warning signs.
steps: Move people and pets into fresh air, without delaying to ventilate or troubleshoot.
Report the alarm, symptoms and possible fuel-burning source to emergency services.
Tell responders about suspected exposure even if symptoms improve outdoors.
Do not reenter until responders say it is safe.
next: Install CO alarms and service heating equipment. Keep generators and grills outdoors, far from openings.
watch: CO is invisible and odorless. A silent smoke alarm is not proof that air is safe.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Leave the building even if responders cannot be reached. Gather outside away from exhaust, keep everyone out and seek reachable medical care for symptoms. Do not send someone back inside to ventilate or switch equipment off.
household: Children, sleeping people and people with limited mobility may not recognize symptoms or reach fresh air independently. Assign evacuation help in advance and keep functioning CO alarms near sleeping areas. Do not make a symptomatic person drive.
pack_now: Prioritize supplies named in this guide that are usable by the person who needs them. Keep the checklist and relevant contact details accessible. Check carrying capacity, storage and equipment instructions in advance; collecting equipment must not delay the immediate protective action.
faqs: Can I turn off the appliance first?

Move everyone to fresh air before investigating. A fuel-burning appliance may continue exposing people while it is being inspected. Call from outside and do not reenter until the hazard has been assessed by appropriate qualified personnel.
Can the household sleep elsewhere inside?

Changing rooms is not a reliable answer to a suspected CO exposure. Get outside to fresh air and seek medical evaluation for symptoms. Keep people together so confusion, faintness or worsening breathing is noticed.
scope: Civilian educational guidance. Linked references may use U.S. emergency systems; local warning methods, laws, services and conditions differ.
